blocks.text: Chaupai:
Now I entreat my readers to go through the episode about Anandpur Sahib, Let us now proceed towards the remaining account of the Khalsa Panth.
How did the conflict develop between the Panth and the hill chiefs? Its detailed description would make this epic very unwieldy. (1)
lines: How did the conflict develop between the Panth and the hill chiefs?
Its detailed description would make this epic very unwieldy.

blocks.text: As the epic "Gur Bilas" has given a detailed description of fit, I would wish to narrate what has not been mentioned in that epic. I desist from describing all the incidents in great detail, For the fear of this epic becoming too voluminous. (2)
lines: As the epic "Gur Bilas" has given a detailed description of fit,
I would wish to narrate what has not been mentioned in that epic.
I desist from describing all the incidents in great detail,
For the fear of this epic becoming too voluminous.

blocks.text: Whosoever is interested in reading things in minute detail, He should delve deeply into the contents of "Gur Bilas". I would just make a passing reference to those incidents, In order to maintain the earlier and latter incidences in a sequence. (3)
lines: Whosoever is interested in reading things in minute detail,
He should delve deeply into the contents of "Gur Bilas".
I would just make a passing reference to those incidents,
In order to maintain the earlier and latter incidences in a sequence.

blocks.text: Dohra:

When Satguru Guru Gobind Singh picked up the sword, For the promotion and expansion of the Khalsa Panth, His commitment to the Khalsa Panth increased manifold. Leaving all other considerations behind and aside. (4)
lines: When Satguru Guru Gobind Singh picked up the sword,
For the promotion and expansion of the Khalsa Panth,
His commitment to the Khalsa Panth increased manifold.
Leaving all other considerations behind and aside.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Khalsa Panth became such a main priority for the Guru, That he started offering his every valuable possession to the Panth. Wherever there were Sikh seats managed by the Masand Mewaras1 , The Tenth Guru despatched the initiated Singhs to replace them. (5)
lines: Khalsa Panth became such a main priority for the Guru,
That he started offering his every valuable possession to the Panth.
Wherever there were Sikh seats managed by the Masand Mewaras1 ,
The Tenth Guru despatched the initiated Singhs to replace them.

blocks.text: All the offerings made at the Gurudwaras as well as before the Gurus, Were transferred to the Khalsa Panth along with the right to Prayer. The entire treasury, the custody of land along with all oher valuables, Were ordered to be handed over to the Khalsa Panth. (6)
lines: All the offerings made at the Gurudwaras as well as before the Gurus,
Were transferred to the Khalsa Panth along with the right to Prayer.
The entire treasury, the custody of land along with all oher valuables,
Were ordered to be handed over to the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Masand Mewras were ordered to get themselves initiated as Singhs, Else they would be deprived of both their status and life as well. Such a decree incensed the masands to such an extent, As if they had been bruised with a sharp-edged dagger. (7)
lines: Masand Mewras were ordered to get themselves initiated as Singhs,
Else they would be deprived of both their status and life as well.
Such a decree incensed the masands to such an extent,
As if they had been bruised with a sharp-edged dagger.

blocks.text: These masands conspired and complained to Mata Gujri, That the Guru had lost his wits and turned insane. The Guru was squandering away the treasury to the Singhs, How could these Singhs capture political power of the country? (8)
lines: These masands conspired and complained to Mata Gujri,
That the Guru had lost his wits and turned insane.
The Guru was squandering away the treasury to the Singhs,
How could these Singhs capture political power of the country?

blocks.text: How could the rustic Jat peasants be made the rulers? How could the lamb-hearted rustics vanquish the lion-hearted Mughals? How could the timid sparrows kill the ferocious Hawks? How could the rustic Jat peasants manage political power? (9)
lines: How could the rustic Jat peasants be made the rulers?
How could the lamb-hearted rustics vanquish the lion-hearted Mughals?
How could the timid sparrows kill the ferocious Hawks?
How could the rustic Jat peasants manage political power?

blocks.text: Dohra:

If this activity ever came to the notice of the Mughal emperor, He would despatch the Mughal army to crush this movement. There would be hardly any place for the Guru to seek refuge, And the Mughals would capture and execute all his followers. (10)
lines: If this activity ever came to the notice of the Mughal emperor,
He would despatch the Mughal army to crush this movement.
There would be hardly any place for the Guru to seek refuge,
And the Mughals would capture and execute all his followers.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Guru's mother, accepting and agreeing with the masands' opinion, Also approved of the masands' version to be true. Calling a meeting of all the officials and custodians of Guru's seats, The masands declared that the Guru had turned insane. (11)
lines: The Guru's mother, accepting and agreeing with the masands' opinion,
Also approved of the masands' version to be true.
Calling a meeting of all the officials and custodians of Guru's seats,
The masands declared that the Guru had turned insane.

blocks.text: Since the day the Guru had invoked the Goddess chandi2 , The Guru had been struck with the chandi's curse and wrath. Since the Guru had picked up a strife with the rulers, They would capture and slaughter all of Guru's Singhs. (12)
lines: Since the day the Guru had invoked the Goddess chandi2 ,
The Guru had been struck with the chandi's curse and wrath.
Since the Guru had picked up a strife with the rulers,
They would capture and slaughter all of Guru's Singhs.

blocks.text: Then all the assembled masands agreed upon a solution, That Sahibzada Jujhar Singh3 be anointed as the Guru, Hearing this conspiracy, Guru Gobind Singh felt outraged, And declared that all the masands had gone mad. (13)
lines: Then all the assembled masands agreed upon a solution,
That Sahibzada Jujhar Singh3 be anointed as the Guru,
Hearing this conspiracy,
Guru Gobind Singh felt outraged,
And declared that all the masands had gone mad.

blocks.text: When the masands were struck by such a perverted thought, They also got a copy of the sacred Guru Granth Sahib burnt. They also got their own place of worship constructed at a place, Where they had committed such a heinous deed. (14)
lines: When the masands were struck by such a perverted thought,
They also got a copy of the sacred Guru Granth Sahib burnt.
They also got their own place of worship constructed at a place,
Where they had committed such a heinous deed.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They disintegrated the Sikh congregations at many places, And merged these splintered groups into their own following. When the Guru came to hear about such a development, He ordered an immediate execution of the masands. (15)
lines: They disintegrated the Sikh congregations at many places,
And merged these splintered groups into their own following.
When the Guru came to hear about such a development,
He ordered an immediate execution of the masands.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When the Singhs received such a decree from the Guru, They massacred and burnt alive all the masands. Some were slaughtered; some were buried alive in walls, Still others were dragged and roasted in cauldrons of boiling oil. (16)
lines: When the Singhs received such a decree from the Guru,
They massacred and burnt alive all the masands.
Some were slaughtered; some were buried alive in walls,
Still others were dragged and roasted in cauldrons of boiling oil.

blocks.text: Dohra:

If I write a more detailed account of this incident, It will increase the volume of this epic still more. The more inquisitive readers should search into the pages of "Gur Bilas". In order to satisfy their curiosity for more details. (17)
lines: If I write a more detailed account of this incident,
It will increase the volume of this epic still more.
The more inquisitive readers should search into the pages of "Gur Bilas".
In order to satisfy their curiosity for more details.
